difficulty.notes: The 9-xiaomi capture (unlike 8-xiaomi) is NOT string-array obfuscated: the AES encryptor Q lives in a dedicated crypto chunk (crypto.17efe504.chunk.js), exposed as encryptAes()->Q and called as d.encryptAes()({user}) from the 2395 login chunk (lazy import of module 23963). The sibling RSA encryptor B (rsa()->B) builds encryptedParams too but is not the username AES path. Cross-file: anchor in the crypto chunk, call site in the 2395 chunk.

task_contract.anchor_definition: The AES encryptor Q that builds encryptedParams for the username; not the encryptAes accessor, the RSA encryptor B, or the login call site.

behavior_category.subtype: AES of username into the encryptedParams request field
behavior_category.recompute_check: AES key/iv parsing is internal; not asserted to a fixed value here

near_categories.why_not: A single credential field (username) is tokenized; this is per-field token derivation.
The value is AES of user input, not a device/browser digest.

evidence: The AES encryptor is one of two functions (Q vs B) in a dedicated crypto chunk reached by lazy import; the call site is in another chunk.
Two encryptors Q (AES) and B (RSA) both return encryptedParams; the username uses the AES one.
The encryptor is reached through encryptAes() accessor and a regenerator-compiled async login handler.

provenance.label_points_to: an older build (ccd23f99); the captured username encryptor is Q in crypto.17efe504.chunk.js, reached from 2395.988a36fc.chunk.js
